experiment: profile reparameterisation with PREDICTED anchors -- no GT anywhere
setup: anchor indices chosen per contour from TRAINING-fold error only; population arc-length profile from training folds only; anchors keep their predicted positions; interior placed at profile positions along the predicted polyline, piecewise between consecutive anchors
why: The k=4 oracle at 0.536mm was entirely the GT anchors. Real anchors carry 1.0-2.5mm error, and reparameterising between erroneous anchors propagates that error onto interior landmarks that were individually better placed than the reparameterisation makes them.

per_landmark_floor.note: all 10 sub-0.8mm landmarks are in CONCHA, the contour where the profile does not apply

bar: Anchors need roughly 0.57-0.83mm for the k=2 gain to survive. On inner_helix and sup._antihelix the BEST landmark any model achieves is 0.99 and 1.09mm, so no anchor currently clears the bar on the two contours where the constraint applies.
conclusion: The arc-length profile is a real population constant (sd 0.12-0.32mm on two contours) but it is NOT exploitable at current localisation accuracy. It becomes exploitable only if selected landmarks reach sub-0.8mm, which no architecture tried here has done on those contours.
